title: The budget lives in Redis as a token bucket, not in process memory
context: RFC 001 sketched an in-process sliding window. It cannot satisfy I3, because process memory is lost on restart and a blocked address goes free immediately. It also breaks I2 in practice behind more than one instance, since each instance would hold a separate budget for the same address and the effective limit would multiply by the instance count.
options: In-process sliding window, as RFC 001 sketched
Redis token bucket keyed by address
Sticky routing by address so a single instance owns each budget
outcome: Redis token bucket keyed by address. It survives a restart because the bucket is not in the process, and it holds one budget per address across every instance. Sticky routing was rejected because it makes the limit correct only while routing is healthy, and a rebalance silently doubles the effective limit with nothing failing loudly.
